- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80.0), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates by 1–3% in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is positive; apply a “lag correction” to subtract 0.5–1.0% from first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low positive values, model tends to underestimate; apply a “sentiment floor” rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment average < 0.33 over last 5 days.
